comment: Security review 2026-10, root cause A §5 (branch A1b). HAND-AUTHORED decision rows for the item-home invariants, written from the design text, graded against the functions production calls: core ItemHome (SyncEngine), web vault/itemhome.ts (store.ts) and extension/src/itemhome.ts (background.ts). Ids are opaque symbols: P = the vault this device holds the item in, S = another vault (one the server or a colluding co-member keys), X/Y/Z = itemIds. home(itemId) is the vaultId of the FIRST envelope this device applied for that itemId (device-local; a fresh device's first home is the server's choice, a stated residual). Sections: admit (one row against a home), pulls (a pull's rows in order: per-row verdicts, the homes after, the single wrong-vault anomaly, and which flagged rows reach materialization), conflict (INV-CONFLICT), serverItem (the push-side copy from a displaced value), edit (INV-EDIT) and seal (the INV-SEAL home cross-check every item seal for a push runs). A9 (security review 2026-10): home(itemId) is recorded ONLY from a row this device actually APPLIED — admit rows carry `applies` (default true; false = a tombstone, a vault whose key this device does not hold, or an envelope that does not open) and an unhomed row that cannot be applied is `skip`: no home, no anomaly, and the row's own handling (a tombstone deletes nothing it never had; ciphertext may be kept for a later key) proceeds. Pull rows express it as `deleted` / `unheld`.

admit.name: no home yet: the row's vault becomes the home
a row under the home applies
a row under another vault is quarantined
a tombstone under another vault is quarantined too (it is a row like any other)
a tombstone under the home applies
A9: no home yet, but the row cannot be applied here (a tombstone): no home is recorded
A9: no home yet, but the row cannot be applied here (a vault this device holds no key for): no home is recorded
A9: a row under the home applies even when it cannot be opened here (a tombstone under the home)
A9: a row under another vault is quarantined whether or not it could be applied

pulls.name: §5.3 fixture, flagged row FIRST, on a device that holds X in P
§5.3 fixture, genuine row FIRST, on a device that holds X in P
residual: on a FRESH device the server chooses the first home (flagged row first)
residual: on a FRESH device the server chooses the first home (genuine row first)
a served tombstone under the wrong vault does not delete X
several wrong-vault rows in one pull raise ONE anomaly
an honest pull: new items take their homes, a flagged row at home materializes, nothing is refused
A9: on a FRESH device a tombstone served FIRST never homes X; the genuine live row then takes the home
A9: on a FRESH device a row under a vault this device holds NO key for, served FIRST, never homes X
A9: an unheld or tombstone row that comes AFTER the home is still quarantined (it names another vault)
A9: a tombstone under the home applies (X is deleted, the home stays)

conflict.name: twin and home agree with the flagged row: materialize from decrypt(flagged)
the A-4 shape: an in-memory twin in P, a flagged row under S: abort, no push
the twin agrees but the home does not: abort (INV-HOME's second lock)

serverItem.name: the displaced value of the item we wrote, in the vault we wrote it to: copy it there
a displaced value under another vault than the pushed one: abort
pushed and losing agree but the home is elsewhere: abort
a fresh id with no home yet: copy

edit.name: the editor's vault is the home: save
the item changed vaults since the editor opened: refuse, never re-target
no home recorded (a queued-only new item's first edit): save under the editor's vault
an edit that names no editor vault is a programming error

seal.name: a fresh id (copy, import row, new item, conflict copy) takes the provenance vault as its home
a seal of X under any other vault is refused
